name: elf_directories
description: Read what pe_info does not say about an ELF file, through checked ranges, never running it. Program headers: every segment (type, flags, offset, addresses, sizes, alignment), the interpreter, whether the stack is executable (PT_GNU_STACK) and whether RELRO is asked for; a segment that runs past the end of the file is a problem. Dynamic array, found through PT_DYNAMIC so a file whose section headers are stripped or damaged is read the same way (through an SHT_DYNAMIC section only when there is no program header table): every tag and its value, the strings of NEEDED, SONAME, RPATH, RUNPATH, FILTER and AUXILIARY, and FLAGS, FLAGS_1, BIND_NOW, SYMBOLIC and TEXTREL decoded; a file with no DT_NEEDED says zero, a file with no dynamic array says it has none, and an array with no DT_NULL before the end of its segment is a problem. Symbols: .dynsym (through DT_SYMTAB, its count from DT_HASH, else from DT_GNU_HASH when the table implies one, else from the section header; a DT_GNU_HASH table with no symbol in any bucket gives only a lower bound, so with no other source the answer is partial and says the table holds at least that many; a disagreement between sources is a problem) and .symtab (only a section header locates it, so a stripped file has none): every row with name, value, size, type, binding, visibility and section index. Notes: every note of the PT_NOTE segments (of the SHT_NOTE sections when there is no program header table) with the GNU build ID and ABI tag read and the others given by owner, type and size. A table range that runs past the end of the file is a problem and the rows that are there are read; it is never an empty list. Every table is the first `limit` rows of the answer, and a longer table is written whole to a file named in `all_results`. Every key and every value of the answer and of each file it names passes the sanitiser and then a backstop (the same shared blocks as pe_directories): a string out of the file is withheld by shape only (a secret of another shape is printed: read a file whose secrets matter in a job with secret_output; the whole only with write_values there), a string whose address points into the middle of a token run is sanitised whole and its head withheld, one longer than 2,048 characters is given by length only, a name longer than 512 characters is given by length, and no list in the answer is longer than the larger of limit and 100 items. The GNU build ID is shown whole: it is the linker's claim about a build, not a secret. A symbolic link, a pipe or a device is refused, and a tool-output directory reached through a symbolic link is refused. Not read: sections, relocations, symbol versions, DWARF, the contents of notes other than the build ID and the ABI tag, any signature or hash (nothing is verified) and anything about what code does. The file of withheld names stops growing at 64 MiB (a limit, with the number of names withheld). The clock is looked at every 65,536 words of a hash table, every 1,024 program or section headers and every 16 symbol rows. Every answer carries status, problems, limits_hit and coverage; a budget that is reached is a limit. A stop signal (SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP) ends it with one JSON answer and the exit code 128 plus the signal from the moment the module has run as far as its stop handlers, which are installed at module level and not when main() starts; a second signal does nothing while the first is answered, and no hidden temporary file is left. A name, a path, a URL or a message that quotes a credential is withheld with the identifier-shaped strings, from version 3: a value given to a password, token, secret or cookie name (password=..., Pwd=..., a Cookie header), a Name/Value pair in text whose Name is a credential (a number, an array or a long Value too, and the NewValue after an OldValue), a -Password style switch, the argument of ConvertTo-SecureString, curl -u user:pass, mysql -uUSER -pSECRET, a bcrypt hash and the known token families; the text is replaced by a marker that holds only its length. Before, only identifier-shaped strings (tokens, key ids, user-info) were withheld, so these were printed. Known gaps: a pair whose Value is an array nested in another or longer than 4,096 characters, a crypt hash that is not bcrypt, and a secret that has neither a credential name nor a token shape.

path.description: An ELF file (executable, shared object, relocatable, core)

write_values.description: Write each dynamic string and the real name behind every withheld name whole to elf-directories-values.jsonl under $OUT (default false; refused outside a job; run the job with secret_output: true)

limit.description: Rows of one table kept in the answer (default 1000, at most 20000: a larger number is refused, as the rows are withheld while the file is read); the whole of a longer table is written to a file and named

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit for reading, in seconds, from 1 to 90 (default 70); a read that reaches it stops, reports what it read and says so. The rows of each table are withheld as they are read, under this limit; the rest of the answer is built after it and has until about 90 s after the call began, at least 5 s after the reading: a string it has no time to check is given by its length and the answer says so (partial). A call that has not answered within 105 s ends with a partial answer of the problems, the limits and the first rows of each table it holds, before the manifest's 120 s limit
